# Release Notes - awake 0.6.0-beta

Release date: 2026-10-23
Package: `awake-daemon.win64.zip`

The sixth beta release of **awake**, a Windows command line tool that keeps
the system awake. This release is about everyday polish: better errors,
documented aliases, faster startup and a build system that carries no local
paths.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project is generated by AI and has not been extensively reviewed.
> Please scrutinize the code carefully before use. The author is not
> responsible or liable for any consequences arising from the use of this
> software.

## Highlights

- **`awake aliases`**: prints every command together with its accepted
  spellings in two aligned columns (also reachable as `awake a` /
  `awake alias`). The help message now has its own "Command aliases" section
  between Usage and Notes instead of a cramped paragraph.
- **Helpful mistakes**: a misspelled command no longer answers with a bare
  "unknown command". The client ranks the known commands by edit distance and
  shows up to three suggestions with their descriptions, for example
  `awake stauts` suggests `awake status`. All arguments are considered, so
  `awake scren of` finds `awake screen off`; a missing subcommand lists the
  available ones. Nothing is executed, and a completely unknown input gets no
  invented suggestion.
- **Atomic configuration writes**: `add`, `del` and `reset` write a temporary
  file and swap it in (`ReplaceFile`), so a daemon reading `awake.ini` at the
  same moment can never see a half-written list.
- **Explainable daemon start failures**: a failed start now reports the Win32
  error code and what to do about it (missing `awake.daemon.exe`, access
  denied because a daemon runs elevated, invalid binary) instead of a generic
  message.
- **Faster startup detection**: the client probes a freshly started daemon
  every 50 ms for the first ten attempts and only then backs off to 250 ms, so
  a healthy start is noticed about 200 ms earlier.
- **Fewer idle costs**: an empty watch list no longer triggers a system-wide
  process snapshot every 30 seconds, and the watch list is matched through a
  set lookup instead of a nested loop.
- **Build scripts without local paths**: `utils\build.bat` and
  `utils\pubrelease.bat` are now thin launchers for PowerShell 7 scripts. The
  toolchain (Visual Studio, Windows SDK, CMake, generator, 7-Zip, Git) is
  resolved from `utils\toolchain.ini` / `%APPDATA%\awake\toolchain.ini`,
  detected automatically, or asked for once and remembered; nothing is
  hard-coded any more. The build falls back to the NMake generator when the
  Visual Studio generator cannot run.
- **One version number**: `version.h` is generated from the single
  `project(VERSION ...)` declaration in `CMakeLists.txt`, so the client and
  the daemon can no longer disagree with the release they came from.

## Fixes

- `awake status` no longer warns "the daemon did not report its version" when
  the daemon is simply not running; the version check only happens while a
  daemon is reachable.

## Behaviour changes

- `awake aliases` is treated like `help` and `version`: it works before the
  first-run license is accepted, because it only prints documentation.
- Unknown commands and misspelled subcommands still exit with status 1, but
  now print a suggestion block.

## Full command list

```
awake help              Show the help message.
awake version           Show the version.
awake aliases           Show every command alias.
awake 0                 Disable keep-awake.
awake 1                 Enable keep-awake (blocks idle sleep/hibernation).
awake status            Show daemon, keep-awake, screen, autostart and
                        watch list status.
awake screen on         Keep the screen on (blocks screen off, screensaver
                        and idle lock).
awake screen off        Stop keeping the screen on.
awake daemon on         Start the background daemon.
awake daemon off        Stop the background daemon.
awake daemon enable     Start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake daemon disable    Do not start the daemon automatically at logon.
awake reload            Re-read the configuration file immediately.
awake reset             Reset the configuration file (asks for
                        confirmation).
awake add <imagename>   Add an image name to the watch list.
awake del <imagename>   Remove an image name from the watch list.
```

See `awake aliases` for the shorthand forms of these commands.

## Installation

1. Extract `awake.exe` and `awake.daemon.exe` from this package into any
   folder. Both executables are statically linked and have no runtime
   dependencies.
2. Run `awake daemon on` (or simply `awake 1`) to start using the tool.
   The configuration file `awake.ini` is created next to the executables on
   first use; the first command also asks for the license.
3. Optional: run `awake daemon enable` to start the daemon automatically at
   every logon.

## Notes

- Keep-awake and screen keep-awake states live in the daemon's memory only;
  after a daemon restart they are inactive again.
- The daemon sends a one-shot stay-awake notification when it starts,
  regardless of the current settings.
- Building from source needs PowerShell 7; set `AWAKE_SDK_ROOT` or use
  `utils\toolchain.ini` when the toolchain is not in a default location.
- This is a beta release; the behaviour and the command line interface may
  still change in incompatible ways before 1.0.
